summary: Tested live Vimeo watch time end to end with real headless Vimeo playback of lesson l-3zyafu0 in course 384eef11de47. Backend: 3/3 pytest pass. The video POST returns spans and duration (421). Segments [[0,10]] and then [[10,20]] merged to [[0,20]] with percent 5. A skip to [[300,400]] was clipped by the budget. The course GET returns video_spans, video_duration and video_percent, and they match what was saved. 401 without auth and 422 for duration 0. Frontend had a CRITICAL bug, which I found and fixed: watch time dropped back to 0:00 after every 5s save. After the fix, video-watch-time goes up about 1s per second ('0:15 of 7:01' ... '0:30 of 7:01'). video-percent matches round(s/421*100). POST .../video fires every 5s and on pause. The saved time stays after reload (0:14, then 0:38 of 7:01, plus 'resumed from'). Seeking to about 5:00 did not jump the watch time; only played seconds were counted.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED. The watch time reset to 0:00 after every save. Cause: `useEffect(() => () => { alive.current = false; }, [])` runs its cleanup during the React StrictMode dev double-mount, so alive.current stayed false forever. onUpdate then returned early, server.current.spans was never updated, and live() only counted the new pending segments. The server still saved correctly. Fix: `useEffect(() => { alive.current = true; return () => { alive.current = false; }; }, [])`.

issues: On first play with no saved progress, the total shows '7:00' because the player duration 420.5 is floored. After the first save it becomes '7:01' (server duration 421). Small inconsistency.

action_items: Review and keep the alive-ref fix in TrackedVideo.jsx. Without it the feature is broken in dev/preview (StrictMode).
Optional: use Math.round, or the server duration from video_meta, so the total label doesn't switch from 7:00 to 7:01.

Optional: flush() takes segments out of pending before the request finishes, so live() leaves out in-flight seconds until the response arrives. This can cause a brief 1-2s dip in the shown time when the network is slow. Consider keeping in-flight segments in live().

TrackedVideo: the inner effect also declares a local variable named `alive`, which shadows the ref. Confusing; consider renaming.
